insight: Recent rain (~5 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: recent rainfall is raising risk by washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; high tide level is raising risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; and hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline. The most recent sample, 6 days ago, was excellent at 5 MPN/100mL.
